title: 8.5 A Command-Aware Hybrid LDO for Advanced HBM Interfaces with 150μA Quiescent Current and 20pF On-Chip Capacitor Achieving Sub-10mV Voltage Droop in 400ps Settling Time
problem: HBM3E/HBM4 interfaces suffer from power-supply-induced jitter (PSIJ) caused by sudden load current surges in write-data-strobe (WDQS) buffers, leading to voltage droop and sampling errors in high-bandwidth memory.
motivation: HBM3E increases to 16 channels and HBM4 to 32 channels for >1TB/s bandwidth, but instantaneous load currents (<100ps edges) create voltage droop on unstable power grids, degrading WDQS jitter and data integrity.
method: When a write command arrives at the memory interface, the voltage regulator gets advance warning and predicts that the write buffers (WDQS) will soon draw a sudden surge of current. To prevent the voltage from dropping too far, the regulator proactively pumps extra current into the circuit just before the surge hits. This prediction-based approach achieves voltage stability within 10mV and settles within 400 picoseconds, while using only 20pF of on-chip energy storage and 150μA of idle power.
key_novelty: By predicting voltage droop from command signals and acting proactively, the regulator maintains sub-10mV stability in 400ps without large on-chip capacitors.
contributions: Command-aware hybrid LDO reducing PSIJ in HBM interfaces
Sub-10mV voltage droop with 20pF on-chip capacitor
400ps settling time for fast WDQS adaptation
limitations: Abstract-only analysis; comparison with other droop-mitigation approaches and broader system impact not discussed.
primary_theme: Command-aware LDO for HBM jitter mitigation
